title.narrative: Advancing Science Diplomacy for Climate and Ocean Risk Resilience in PICTs

description.narrative: This element supports science diplomacy at the intersection of science, policy, and international cooperation to address climate and ocean hazards in Pacific Island Countries (PICs). It contributes to strengthening regional and national scientific capacity while aligning with UNESCO’s global science diplomacy priorities to advance sustainable development, resilience, and informed decision-making. Pacific Island Countries face disproportionate exposure to climate and ocean-related hazards, including tsunamis, coastal inundation, and extreme weather events, while possessing limited scientific infrastructure and technical capacity. Science diplomacy offers a mechanism to: • Bridge scientific and policy gaps • Strengthen equitable access to scientific cooperation • Enhance regional representation in global science-policy dialogues This element aligns with the priorities identified through the 2025 UNESCO Global Ministerial Dialogue on Science Diplomacy, particularly: • Equitable collaboration on emerging technologies • Responsible management of shared ocean and natural resources • Protection of science systems in crisis contexts
